title: Rice researchers to use NASA AI model to improve hurricane risk estimates
key_facts: Rice University researchers Avantika Gori and Guha Balakrishnan are developing an open-source tool built on NASA's Prithvi-WxC AI weather and climate model (developed with IBM) to simulate thousands of potential tropical cyclones.
The project is titled 'Leveraging Large Earth Foundation Models for Probabilistic Hurricane Hazard Assessment'.

Major storms are rare, so insurers and researchers have limited historical data on how often and how severely they cause losses; an average Atlantic season has 14 named storms, seven hurricanes and three major hurricanes (NOAA).
The team aims to build a dataset of about 10,000 synthetic cyclones, refined with physics-informed models to estimate wind and rainfall.
The tool is also designed to test hurricane hazard under different climate scenarios and could later be adapted to other natural hazards.
The work targets the insurance protection gap and is run with CERCat, an industry consortium of Rice and Lehigh Universities.
The release reports no results yet; the researchers say they will test how many storms the tool can generate and plan to make it open source.
quote_evidence: AI gives us an opportunity to explore thousands of realistic storms that history alone cannot provide,” said Gori
To expand that record, the Rice team aims to develop a dataset of about 10,000 synthetic cyclones.
The research team plans to make the tool open source so others can examine, use and build on the framework.
why_it_matters_hint: Computer-made storms could give insurers and planners a fuller picture of rare, severe hurricanes than the short historical record allows.
